role: Political adviser (Reform Party group in Tallinn City Council, party office, Reform group in the Riigikogu)
description: Adviser to the Reform group in Tallinn City Council (1996–1999), adviser to the party (1999) and to the Reform group in the Riigikogu (1999–2001), according to Estonian Wikipedia, citing his government biography.

role: Adviser and head of office to Minister Toivo Asmer; adviser to Prime Minister Siim Kallas
description: Adviser and head of office of minister Toivo Asmer (2001–2002), then in 2002 adviser on domestic and organisational matters to Prime Minister Siim Kallas.
Head of the administration of Tallinn's city-centre district.

English Wikipedia gives 2003–2011; Estonian Wikipedia gives 2003 and 2007–2011. In 2012 Michal said he had raised donations for the party as secretary general 'for eight years'. Chairman of the party council from June 2011 and of the party's Tallinn organisation from January 2014, according to Estonian Wikipedia.

role: Member of Tallinn City Council (Tallinna Linnavolikogu); Reform group chairman
description: Council member in 1999–2001 and again after the 2009 election (Estonian Wikipedia); led the Reform list in the 2017 and 2021 Tallinn elections. His 2023 campaign page described him as head of Reform's Tallinn region and chairman of its council group, and listed goals as deputy chairman of the council for 2021–2025. The end date is approximate (his entry into the government in April 2023).

role: Member of the Riigikogu (X Riigikogu, substitute member)
description: Sat in the X Riigikogu in 2004–2005 and in 2006 as a substitute member. Elected to the XI Riigikogu in 2007, he chose to remain the party's secretary general instead, according to Estonian Wikipedia.

organization: Government of Estonia (Andrus Ansip's third cabinet)
description: Resigned after the 'Silvergate' party-financing affair, announcing his decision on 6 December 2012; succeeded by Hanno Pevkur.

role: Member of the Riigikogu (XII, XIII and XIV Riigikogu)
description: Sat in the Riigikogu from December 2012, after leaving the government, to 2015 and again between his ministerial posts until 2023 (Estonian Wikipedia). Estonian Wikipedia states that he chaired the Reform faction in 2014–2015 and again from 2016; his 2023 campaign page says he chaired the Riigikogu's Economic Affairs Committee at the end of the XIV Riigikogu. Re-elected in 2023, he gave up the seat to join the government.

role: Minister of Economic Affairs and Infrastructure (majandus- ja taristuminister)
organization: Government of Estonia (Taavi Rõivas's second cabinet)
description: Left office when the Rõivas government fell after a successful no-confidence vote in November 2016. His campaign page cites a 'zero bureaucracy' initiative with business organisations and the operation to bring passengers home after the collapse of Estonian Air.

organization: Government of Estonia (Kaja Kallas's third cabinet)
description: Minister of climate and the living environment in Kaja Kallas's third government; as minister he exercised the state's shareholder role in the airline Nordica (see polemics). Nominated in June–July 2024 by the Reform Party to succeed Kallas as prime minister.

Nominated by the Reform Party after Kaja Kallas was chosen as EU High Representative; designated by President Karis, authorised by the Riigikogu on 22 July 2024 (64 votes to 27) and sworn in with his cabinet on 23 July 2024. Reform–Estonia 200–SDE coalition until March 2025, then Reform–Estonia 200; a minority government since August 2026.
Elected at the party's general assembly with 664 votes, out of 818 members taking part.
